## Community Coordinated Modeling Center Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information ( CCMC DONKI )
## Message Type: Space Weather Notification - CMEs (Mars, OSIRIS-APEX, Parker Solar Probe)
##
## Message Issue Date: 2024-05-16T23:48:41Z
## Message ID: 20240516-AL-008
##
## Disclaimer: NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center is the United States Government official source for space weather forecasts. This "Experimental Research Information" consists of preliminary NASA research products and should be interpreted and used accordingly.


## Summary:

Multiple CMEs have been detected as follows:
1: O-type CME detected by STEREO A / SOHO. 

Start time of the event: 2024-05-16T01:25Z.

Estimated speed: ~1103 km/s.

Estimated opening half-angle: 22 deg.

Direction (lon./lat.): 105/0 in Heliocentric Earth Equatorial coordinates.

Activity ID: 2024-05-16T01:25:00-CME-001

2: C-type CME detected by STEREO A / SOHO. 

Start time of the event: 2024-05-16T04:36Z.

Estimated speed: ~773 km/s.

Estimated opening half-angle: 16 deg.

Direction (lon./lat.): 112/-6 in Heliocentric Earth Equatorial coordinates.

Activity ID: 2024-05-16T04:36:00-CME-001

3: O-type CME detected by STEREO A / SOHO. 

Start time of the event: 2024-05-16T06:48Z.

Estimated speed: ~1110 km/s.

Estimated opening half-angle: 21 deg.

Direction (lon./lat.): 109/-1 in Heliocentric Earth Equatorial coordinates.

Activity ID: 2024-05-16T06:48:00-CME-001

Based on preliminary analysis by the Moon to Mars Space Weather Analysis Office and heliospheric modeling carried out at NASA Community Coordinated Modeling Center, it is estimated that the CMEs may impact Mars, OSIRIS-APEX, and Parker Solar Probe. The leading edge of the CMEs will reach Mars at 2024-05-19T05:08Z, OSIRIS-APEX at 2024-05-18T07:17Z, and Parker Solar Probe at 2024-05-17T14:47Z (plus minus 7 hours).

## Notes: 


SCORE CME typification system:
S-type: CMEs with speeds less than 500 km/s
C-type: Common 500-999 km/s
O-type: Occasional 1000-1999 km/s
R-type: Rare 2000-2999 km/s
ER-type: Extremely Rare >3000 km/s
